source_caption:
Richard Linklater, Ethan Hawke, and Julie Delpy crafted one of the most agonizingly perfect, breathless romantic sequences in cinematic history by daring to let the clock run out. Unfolding entirely in real-time, the film’s mounting, intoxicating tension culminates in a cramped Parisian apartment. As Delpy effortlessly sways to Nina Simone and casually warns, “Baby, you are gonna miss that plane,” Hawke’s quiet, deeply resigned “I know” masterfully cuts to black. It is a profoundly bold, brilliantly ambiguous cliffhanger that completely trusts its audience, proving that true romantic gravity isn’t found in massive, sweeping declarations, but in the quiet, undeniable realization that you simply cannot walk away a second time.
⠀
Before Sunset (2004), directed by Richard Linklater, starring Ethan Hawke, Julie Delpy. Nine years after a brief, life-altering encounter in Vienna, an American author and a French environmentalist suddenly cross paths again in Paris, spending a single, fleeting afternoon desperately navigating their lingering regrets, unfulfilled longing, and the rapidly closing window of time before his flight departs.

source_details.title: Before Sunset
source_details.synopsis: Before Sunset is a 2004 American romantic drama film directed by Richard Linklater, who co-wrote the screenplay with Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy, from a story by Linklater and Kim Krizan. It is the first film by Warner Independent Pictures. The sequel to Before Sunrise (1995) and the second installment in the Before trilogy, Before Sunset follows Jesse (Hawke) and Céline (Delpy) as they reunite nine years later in Paris. Linklater, Krizan, Hawke, and Delpy began developing a larger budget sequel in the 1990s, but failed to secure funding to begin production.
